skill.name: directory-submissions
skill.description: Plan directory submissions for startup, SaaS, AI, agent, and no-code launches. The skill helps assess readiness, choose directory tiers, prepare positioning variants, and track backlink progress.
skill.summary: Plan directory submissions, launch listings, review drives, and backlink tracking for software products.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

content.user_title: Plan Directory Submissions for Product Launches
content.value_statement: Directory launches often fail because teams submit before pages, assets, and reviews are ready. This skill creates a staged submission plan with positioning, tracking, and follow-up actions.
actual_capabilities: Runs a launch readiness assessment before recommending submissions.
Selects relevant directory tiers for SaaS, AI, agent, MCP, no-code, and review sites.
Builds a Product Hunt preparation timeline around a launch date.
Creates tier-specific positioning guidance to avoid duplicate directory copy.
Uses a tracker template to manage submission status, live links, and backlink verification.
limitations: It does not submit forms or create directory accounts automatically.
Directory authority, pricing, and policies can change after the reference list was written.
It needs accurate product, audience, asset, and launch-date details from the user.
It cannot guarantee approvals, rankings, backlinks, reviews, or referral traffic.

use_cases.title: Prepare a launch directory plan
use_cases.description: Create a staged submission plan for launch week and the weeks after launch.

use_cases.title: Organize SaaS review listings
use_cases.description: Plan G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, and related listings around a realistic review drive.

use_cases.title: Map AI and MCP directories
use_cases.description: Choose AI tool, agent, and MCP registries only when the product is a strong fit.

prompt_templates.title: Assess readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether our product is ready for directory submissions. Ask only for missing details, then list hard and soft blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Build launch plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Launch planning with a known date
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-week directory submission plan for our product launch on [date]. Include tiers, order, assets, and review tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Create positioning variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Preparing copy for different directory audiences
prompt_templates.prompt: Create distinct directory positioning variants for startup, SaaS, AI, review, and developer directories using our product details.

prompt_templates.title: Audit submission progress
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after submissions are underway
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our directory tracker summary and recommend the next actions. Focus on missing backlinks, weak positioning, and stalled approvals.

output_examples.input: We launch an AI SaaS in three weeks and need a directory plan.
output: A readiness assessment lists missing pages, assets, and review capacity.
A three-week plan prioritizes Product Hunt, startup directories, SaaS directories, and AI directories.
A follow-up checklist covers positioning variants, tracker setup, and review outreach.

output_examples.input: Can we reuse one description for every directory?
output: The response explains why duplicate copy weakens directory performance.
It suggests separate descriptions for startup, SaaS, AI, developer, and review audiences.
It provides practical fields such as tagline, short description, long description, and tags.

output_examples.input: We submitted to fifty directories last week. What should we do next?
output: The response shifts focus from raw submission count to backlink verification and destination pages.
It recommends tracking weekly KPIs, review progress, and organic discovery signals.
It identifies when to improve pages instead of submitting to more directories.

best_practices: Complete landing pages, pricing, policies, screenshots, and demo assets before submitting.
Use different positioning for each directory tier and audience.
Track every submission, approval, live URL, backlink status, and follow-up note.
anti_patterns: Submitting to every directory without checking audience fit.
Copying the same product description into every listing.
Treating a launch spike as a complete distribution strategy.

faq.question: Does this skill submit to directories automatically?
faq.answer: No. It plans submissions and tracking. Users still complete forms and account steps manually.

faq.question: Which products fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits startup, SaaS, AI, agent, MCP, no-code, and software products seeking listings and backlinks.

faq.question: Does it include Product Hunt guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes readiness checks, a preparation timeline, launch-day guidance, and post-launch follow-up.

faq.question: Can it help with G2 and Capterra?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when review listings are useful and how to plan a review drive.

faq.question: Will it guarantee backlinks or traffic?
faq.answer: No. Directory approvals, link attributes, rankings, and referral traffic depend on each platform.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
